headline: Google's Gemini Audio edits out 'ums' and 'ahs' with new AI transcription models
summary: Google's Gemini Audio is getting a major update with new AI transcription models that can automatically detect jargon and remove filler words, while also supporting over 85 languages.
details: Google has updated its Gemini Audio models with new Gemini 3.5 capabilities, including advanced transcription features that can automatically identify specialized jargon and support over 85 languages. These new models, Gemini 3.5 Live, 3.5 Live Experimental, and 3.5 Transcribe, are designed to improve the precision of Google's voice-controlled AI, even in noisy environments or with interrupted speech.

The new Gemini 3.5 Transcribe model is a significant advancement over its predecessor, Chirp 3, particularly in multilingual performance and reducing word error rates. Google states that users can now "edit naturally with just your voice," as the model automatically formats text and removes filler words like "um" and "uh." It also allows for custom vocabularies, adapting transcriptions to unique spellings and jargon, and can attribute speech for up to three speakers in pre-recorded audio with word-level timestamps.

Alongside Transcribe, Google is launching Gemini 3.5 Live and 3.5 Live Experimental. These models build upon the existing speech recognition technology used in Gemini's voice chat. Gemini 3.5 Live offers improved handling of mid-sentence interruptions and language recognition, while Gemini 3.5 Live Experimental provides step-by-step narration of its progress in real time as it tackles complex reasoning tasks.

These Gemini Audio updates are rolling out starting today for all macOS Gemini app users in English. Android users will see the Rambler dictation feature updated in select countries and languages. Developers can access these features in public preview via the Gemini API through AI Studio and Antigravity. Google has also indicated that Chrome support is planned for the near future.
